subject: Quick question on extracting only some iterations from mvSamples

messages.author: 9c2c0c89a3d22b1b
messages.subject: Quick question on extracting only some iterations from mvSamples
parts:
Dear Chris, Daniel, and everyone,

I was wondering if there's a way to extract only some iterations, say the last 10, from a modelValues object, specifically from something like
Cmcmc$mvSamples. The crucial point is to do this without duplicating the whole Monte Carlo output as an intermediate step.

I've read §14.1 of the 1.0.1 manual, and have been experimenting with the indexing explained there, but I'm only managing to choose subsets of variables, rather than subsets of iterations.

If I do something like, say,

subset <- as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)[Cmcmc$mvSamples$getSize()-(9:0),]

then it looks like the whole "as.matrix(Cmcmc$mvSamples)" is first produced as an intermediate step.

I'm working with large Monte Carlo outputs and multiple chains, and pushing the memory limits of what I can do; hence the question.

Cheers!
Luca

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Quick question on extracting only some iterations from mvSamples
parts:
Luca, this is just a quick idea, but I think you could accomplish what you need using the resize() function on the modelValues object (to decrease the number of iterations stored: resize(modelValues, new_size) ), then extract the reduced-size array of samples using as.matrix().  I'm not able to sketch this out fully right now, and you should do some experimenting about how the existing samplers in a modelValues object are retained following a call to resize()... This is a bit of a work-around, and you should verify it's operating the way you want it to.

Cheers,
Daniel

messages.author: 9c2c0c89a3d22b1b
messages.subject: Re: Quick question on extracting only some iterations from mvSamples
parts:
Thank you so much, Daniel!

I wanted to keep the full modelValues object and use just a small part for some computations. But your suggestion made me realize that I would need to duplicate it anyway at some point (with "as.matrix()" or "as.list()") in order to save it to disk. So I'd eventually stumble into a bigger problem anyway.

I think I'll proceed running shorter chains instead, using 'reset=F' and the very convenient 'resetMV=T', so I can do the computations and also manage to save smaller chunks that can be joined afterwards. Nimble has many convenient settings!

By the way, I believe that the "as.list()" conversion option is quite new? Just discovered it in the new manual and I'm really happy about it, exactly what I needed!

Cheers,
Luca

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: Quick question on extracting only some iterations from mvSamples
parts:
Hi Luca,
Glad to see you've got a path ahead.
In case it helps, section 14.1 of the User Manual also shows how you can access elements of a modelValues (e.g. cmcmc$mvSamples) by node name and "row".
The as.list conversion has actually been around for quite a while, but I guess maybe it hasn't had wide exposure so people know about it.
Perry
